caseStudy.title: MosaicMed
caseStudy.background:
MosaicMed offers a retrieval assistant over public product instructions and private partner policy documents. Its AKS API uses workload identity to retrieve endpoint credentials. The team requires that all retrieval and cache operations use verified partner access scope. The service stores no personal medical records.

Recent deployment logs show that the Pods are healthy, but after scaling from two to eight, the PostgreSQL connection budget was exceeded. The maximum pool size is configured per replica. Thirty database connections must remain reserved for other workloads. A new event routing rule should handle updates only under private partner paths.

A recent credential rotation used a versioned secret URI. The process is long-lived and must discover a new secret version without redeploying images.

Reserved for other clients: 30
Maximum API replicas: 8

questions.prompt: Type the Redis SET option used in the frontier command to express a 105-second expiry.
answer: EX
questions.explanation: SET with EX attaches an expiration in seconds as part of the value write.

questions.prompt: An Event Grid subscription should allow only frontier.DocumentAccepted events with subjects under /tenant/frontier/. Which configuration expresses both constraints?
questions.answer: Include event type frontier.DocumentAccepted and set subjectBeginsWith to /tenant/frontier/
questions.explanation: Event-type selection and a subject prefix address separate constraints. Include the ending slash to avoid adjacent prefix matches.
